clue.text: Band is overhead overlooking motorway

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so the motorway letter is ignored

parts.note: an overhead is a smash, the hard downward shot in tennis
M is the label for a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A band rigged above a road, like a gantry banner over a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SMASH and drop its M to get SASH. 'Overhead' reads like a location, but it is the tennis shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a strip of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist, a kind of decorative strap.

clue.text: Reserve mostly shown amid loneliness and anxiety

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of reserve's synonym is dropped
being shown amid something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: solitude is the state of being alone
ice is coolness of manner, reserve; cut short it loses its E

explanation.surface: A shy, isolated person suffers both loneliness and worry, keeping their feelings to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a stock or a substitute player, but here it is ice, the frosty manner of a reserved person.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is concerned care or worry for someone, so it can stand for anxiety felt on another's behalf.

clue.text: Artist boards rickety punts in summery location

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters of the boats are knocked out of order
to board a boat is to get inside it, so the artist goes within the other letters

parts.note: the letters of punts rearranged
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter climbs into wobbly punts on a river on a hot summer day.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered spot that catches and holds warm sunshine, an ideal place on a summer day.

clue.text: This lot need mostly to unwind, socialising in a lively way

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter of need goes
unwinding loosens something tightly ordered, so the letters come apart and regroup

parts.note: taken as written
need without its final D

explanation.surface: A stressed group of people needs a chance to relax and enjoy themselves at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of THIS LOT NEE are reshuffled into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out on the tiles is an informal idiom for a night of wild partying and carousing, like cats on rooftops.

clue.text: Standard gold kept in New Mexico by gangster

indicators.note: something kept in a place is held inside it, so gold sits within the state's letters

parts.note: NM is the postal abbreviation for New Mexico
or is gold in heraldry
Al Capone is the crossword's stock gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster stashes his usual gold in a New Mexico hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal is standard or ordinary, conforming to the usual pattern or level.

clue.text: Novelist draining last short drink round hotel has difficulty

indicators.note: draining the last means emptying out the final bit, so the novelist's surname loses its end

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, author of Tess, without his final Y

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the drink's letters go about the hotel letter

parts.note: a sip is a small mouthful of a drink
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer finishes off his drink in a hotel bar and is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short drink' looks like a measure of spirits, but it is simply a small mouthful.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering or severe privation, a state of being up against real difficulty.

clue.text: Bill upset club

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the club's word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a bill at their club.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is an informal word for a running bill, as in a bar tab paid at the end of the night.

clue.text: Grotesque character given name has support when speaking?

definitions.note: a thing that gives support, a noun

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter, the cannibal of The Silence of the Lambs
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A monstrous villain, once named, needs backing when talking.
explanation.walkthrough: LECTER plus N; the question mark flags that support here is physical, a stand for notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a sloping stand holding a speaker's notes, so it literally props things up during a speech.

clue.text: Stamp showing marine animal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an official mark pressed into wax or paper
second meaning: a flippered mammal of the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp' suggests a postage stamp picturing a sea creature; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an embossed official emblem pressed onto documents and a sleek flippered mammal that basks on rocks.

clue.text: Official brought up difficulty with area cut in review

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised from the bottom, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a rub is a snag, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: a review revises and reworks material, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: the seven letters of area and cut, rearranged

explanation.surface: A council inspector raises a problem about an area that was trimmed in a review.
explanation.walkthrough: RUB reversed is BUR, then AREA CUT rearranged gives EAUCRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat is a government administrator, an official who follows procedure and paperwork.

clue.text: Listlessness in monkey eating first of oranges

indicators.note: something eaten goes inside the eater, so the monkey's letters wrap round the fruit's letter

parts.note: a langur is a long-tailed Asian monkey

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the following word only

parts.note: the first letter of oranges

explanation.surface: A sluggish monkey is found idly snacking on oranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a dreamy lack of energy, a pleasant tiredness or inertia.

clue.text: Care to wander round British city in novel

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters encircle the next pieces
wandering letters stray from their places and end in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of care rearranged
B is the abbreviation for British
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A caring figure roams around a British city in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London postcode, a crossword standby for city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's 1938 gothic novel set at the Cornish house Manderley.

clue.text: Offensive language recurs excessively? Not completely!

indicators.note: not completely means only part of the following words is used, so the answer lies within them

parts.note: found running across the end of recurs and the start of excessively

explanation.surface: Someone complains that swearing keeps coming up far too often, then admits it is not quite that bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse is a swear word, an oath or piece of bad language.

clue.text: A refined group with intelligence receiving Conservative patronage

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so the group's letters hold the party letter

parts.note: taken as written
U means upper class, refined, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
spies gather intelligence
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: An elegant intelligence unit takes in a Tory and enjoys high-level sponsorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their backing, sponsorship or protection.

clue.text: Put fear into friend holding papers

indicators.note: holding something means having it within, so the friend's letters enclose the papers

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend
ID papers are identity documents

explanation.surface: A friend clutching documents comes over as menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate is to frighten or cow someone, especially to make them do what you want.

clue.text: Files etc not moving for hearing

indicators.note: for hearing means as it sounds to a listener, not as it is spelt

parts.note: the word for standing still sounds the same as the word for office supplies

explanation.surface: Office files that are just sitting unmoved, waiting for a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The two spellings, ending -ARY and -ERY, are said identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery covers writing materials and office supplies such as files, paper, envelopes and pens.

clue.text: Better thing that is given round in 80s film

parts.note: to top is to better or beat
a firearm is something loaded with rounds of ammunition

explanation.surface: A better item is passed around in a 1980s movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given round' sounds like being handed around, but a round is a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gun is the 1986 Tom Cruise film about naval fighter pilots.

clue.text: Clear inspector with period of work touring college

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so the stint's letters surround the college letter

parts.note: a stint is a spell of work
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A police inspector's spell on duty takes in a visit to a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means sharply defined and easy to make out, plain or obvious.

clue.text: Recognise mug with distorted pout

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: mug is slang for face
the letters of pout rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a face pulling a twisted sulky expression.
explanation.definitionFit: To face up to something is to acknowledge and accept an unpleasant truth rather than avoid it.

clue.text: Boat service without terminal in Kent town has delay

indicators.note: without its terminal means lacking its last letter, so the end is chopped off
in places the boat service inside the town's letters

parts.note: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, south-east England
a ferry is a boat service; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A ferry missing its final stop in a Kent harbour town is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: FERRY loses its Y and goes inside DEAL. 'Terminal' suggests a ferry terminal, but it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferral is a postponement, putting something off to a later time.

clue.text: One ruling set once collapsed with start of insurrection

parts.note: fell in means caved in, as a roof does

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of insurrection

explanation.surface: A former ruler's regime caved in when an uprising began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling set' suggests a governing clique, but the set is a film set; once says the ruler is dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian film director of La Dolce Vita, and a director commands the film set; he died in 1993.

clue.text: Force top Frenchman to return in middle of site

indicators.note: in puts the reversed chunk inside the central letters
the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of site

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
M is Monsieur, the French for Mr

explanation.surface: A leading Frenchman is forced to come back to the centre of a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Frenchman' looks like a French leader, but top and Frenchman are two separate pieces, reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the force of one body striking another, or a forceful effect.

clue.text: Pair with right to enter sunless island to create illustrations

indicators.note: sunless means without S, the abbreviation for sun, so that letter is taken out
entering means going inside, so the pair and right go into the island

parts.note: Sark, one of the Channel Islands between England and France, without its S
R is the abbreviation for right
a pair is two

explanation.surface: Two people take the right to visit a gloomy island and draw pictures there.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small Channel Island off the coast of Normandy; S is the abbreviation for sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Artwork means pictures and illustrations prepared for a publication.

clue.text: Magnate not coy in flotation?

indicators.note: floating letters drift loose and settle in another order, with a nod to a company floating

parts.note: the six letters of not and coy rearranged

explanation.surface: A business mogul is far from shy when his company floats on the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: A flotation is also the launch of a company on the stock exchange, which suits a magnate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy and powerful business figure, a captain of industry.

clue.text: Imitation could be a form of this contrived lefty art

definitions.text: Imitation could be a form of this

indicators.note: contrived means artificially put together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the eight letters of lefty and art rearranged

explanation.surface: Copying left-wing art is a form of praise, echoing the old proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says imitation is the sincerest form of flattery, so the definition completes a familiar saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that copying someone shows admiration, making imitation a sincere kind of praise.

clue.text: Sign of repetition in pundit tolerated

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: found across the end of pundit and the start of tolerated

explanation.surface: A commentator who keeps repeating himself is put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto marks, a pair of small commas, show that the item above is repeated.

clue.text: Son given rebuke is down

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to wig is an old word for scold, as in a wigging

explanation.surface: A boy who has been told off is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like feeling sad, but it is the verb to down a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To swig is to drink in large gulps, to knock back or gulp a drink.

clue.text: Legal claim reportedly at college produces opinionated piece

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the claim's word is given by its sound

parts.note: a right is a legal entitlement
being up means in residence at a university

explanation.surface: A lawsuit at a university leads to an editorial column.
explanation.walkthrough: Being up at Oxford or Cambridge means being a student there.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a newspaper review or report that gives the writer's judgement on something.

clue.text: Something that's poached say close to fencing

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of fencing

explanation.surface: A poacher creeps near a fence, after game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poached' suggests stolen game by a fence, but it is cooking in simmering water.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg is a classic thing cooked by poaching, cracked into simmering water.

clue.text: Striking wit reduced by half in effect

indicators.note: reduced by half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a wit is a comedian; keep the first four of its eight letters

explanation.surface: A sharp comic remark is cut down to size for effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like an adjective meaning impressive, but it means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is a result or consequence, the effect that follows from something.

clue.text: Advance to get a gin?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: make progress, move forward

definitions.note: a cryptic reading, giving an instruction rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: second, cryptic reading: grinding up the letters of a four-letter word for profit produces the letters of a gin

explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as GAIN, ground up: its letters rearranged spell A GIN. The question mark flags this reverse anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain ground is to make progress or advance, as an army taking territory does.

clue.text: Old Northern entertainer gets approval

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Peter Kay is a comedian from Bolton in the north of England

explanation.surface: A veteran comic from the North wins the audience's approval.
explanation.definitionFit: An okay is an informal noun for assent or sanction, as in giving the go-ahead.
